advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a corpus fixture + assertion for a reply with no parseable JSON object (expected layout 'prose', current_ok=False, new_ok=False).
evidence: _structured_matrix.py:156 "``prose`` — otherwise (a single bare object mid-prose, or no parseable object at all)"
_LAYOUT_GOLDENS only maps layout_prose/fenced/multi_object/quoted_json — layout_prose reply is 'my verdict is {"verdict": "PASS", ...}' i.e. one parseable object, never zero
score_reply's current_ok=new_ok=False outcome (a no-JSON reply) is a headline measured result but is never asserted; only the 1/4→4/4 parse table and the four clean layout classes are pinned
_structured_matrix.py:104-111 _distinct_values dedups by equal Python value; classify_layout:159 branches on len(distinct) >= 2
layout_multi_object.json reply contains two DIFFERENT objects ({"relation":...} and {"verdict":...}), so the dedup path (equal values collapsing to 1) is never exercised
search_files shows _distinct_values referenced only in the source, never in a test
advisory.finding: No test covers classify_layout / score_reply on a reply containing ZERO parseable JSON objects (pure prose, no JSON) — the module docstring names this as the 'prose' fallthrough ("or no parseable object at all"), and it is the most common live failure shape, but every corpus fixture contains at least one parseable object. A regression that mishandled the empty-object case (e.g. IndexError in classify_layout, or wrong current_ok/new_ok) would not be caught offline.
merged_from: The _distinct_values dedup contract — two IDENTICAL top-level JSON objects must NOT classify as 'multi_object' — is untested. The layout_multi_object golden contains two DISTINCT objects (a dep-link record and a verdict), so a regression that removed or broke the dedup (making it a plain count) would still pass the committed tests while silently changing measured layout_counts on real replies that repeat the same object.
scenarios: A live model reply with no JSON at all (pure prose refusal / apology) — the scorer must record it as prose with current_ok=new_ok=False
A refactor to classify_layout that reorders the distinct/spans checks and dereferences spans[0] on an empty list
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a fixture like layout_no_json.json (a pure-prose reply with no braces) and assert classify_layout(text) == 'prose' and score_reply(text, model) == ReplyScore('prose', False, False).

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the harness apply each cell's config_file (per-cell REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE resolution) or assert cell.provider matches the resolved provider before labeling, so scores can never be misattributed.
evidence: `for cell in cells:` then `config = LLMConfig.from_env(repo_root=str(rebar_repo))` (test_structured_output_matrix.py:164-172) — config does not depend on `cell`
`cell.config_file` is defined in `_structured_matrix.py` `Cell` but a search of the harness for `config_file` returns no matches — the field is never applied
Comment claims 'This cell's provider is selected through its committed overlay' (test_structured_output_matrix.py:170-171) but no per-cell overlay is applied
dropped.finding: The live harness iterates over every provider cell but resolves the model config once from the ambient REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE and never uses cell.config_file; results are keyed/labeled by cell.provider while the actual model called is always the arm's configured overlay. If more than one provider credential is present in a single process, replies are attributed to the wrong provider.
scenarios: An operator runs the harness locally with both ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and OPENAI_API_KEY set and a single REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE: both anthropic and openai cells report 'measured', both call the SAME configured model, but the score table labels them as distinct providers.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Compute the budget against the number of CREDENTIALED cells (or count only cells that will be measured), not len(cells), so the cap matches the calls an arm actually makes.
evidence: Only credentialed cells make calls: `if sm.credential_status(cell.provider) == 'unmeasured': ... continue` (test_structured_output_matrix.py:165-167)
Each CI arm supplies only its own provider credential (workflow env guards keyed on matrix.provider), so exactly one cell is measured per arm
dropped.finding: The call-budget check is computed against the full cross-provider matrix (len(cells) providers), but each CI arm only ever measures the ONE cell whose credential is present, so the planned count overstates an arm's real call volume by a factor of the provider count and can raise CallBudgetExceeded for a budget that the arm would not actually exceed.
scenarios: An operator sets max_calls to just above the real per-arm cost (e.g. 40 = 1 cell × 2 variants × 2 prompts × 10 repeats); the budget check computes 120 (3 cells) and refuses the sweep even though the arm would only make 40 calls.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Guard the spans[0] access in classify_layout (or derive both the count and the span from a single scan) so a scanner divergence degrades to 'prose' rather than raising.
evidence: `spans = _object_spans(text)` and `distinct = _distinct_values(_all_json_objects(text))` are computed from two separate scanners (_structured_matrix.py:157-158)
`if len(distinct) == 1: ... start, end, _ = spans[0]` (_structured_matrix.py classify_layout) — unguarded index into spans
_object_spans (imported from _structured_matrix) and _all_json_objects (imported from rebar.llm.structured) are duplicated brace state machines, not one shared function
dropped.finding: classify_layout indexes spans[0] in the single-object branch, relying on _object_spans and _all_json_objects (two independent brace-scan implementations) staying perfectly in lockstep; if they ever diverge such that _all_json_objects yields one distinct value while _object_spans yields none, this raises IndexError instead of falling through to 'prose'.
scenarios: A future edit to either brace scanner (e.g. rebar.llm.structured._all_json_objects) that changes which regions parse could make distinct non-empty while spans is empty, producing an IndexError on a live reply during a paid run.
